problem:
For the twice-differentiable function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ we have the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,0) & =3, & \,{f}^{′}(1,0) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(1,0) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Use the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to approximate the value of $f(1,2).$

activity_context.topic_title: Second-Degree Taylor Polynomials of Multivariable Functions
